A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be a [[Definition:Square Matrix|square matrix]] of [[Definition:Order of Square Matrix|order]] $n$ over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]] $K$.
Then $\lambda \in K$ is an [[Definition:Eigenvalue of Matrix|eigenvalue]] of $\mathbf A$ {{iff}}:
:$\map \det {\mathbf A - \lambda \mathbf I} = 0$

B_source.statement:
Let $\mathbf M$ be a [[Definition:Square Matrix|square matrix]] over a [[Definition:Field (Abstract Algebra)|field]].
Then $\mathbf M$ is [[Definition:Singular Matrix|singular]] {{iff}}:
:$\map \det {\mathbf M} = 0$

substitutions.M singular (has nontrivial kernel): A - lambda I has a nonzero vector v with (A - lambda I)v = 0

validity_conditions: lambda is an eigenvalue iff (A - lambda I)v = 0 for some nonzero v, i.e. iff A - lambda I has nontrivial kernel, i.e. is singular.
The singular <=> det = 0 criterion applied to M = A - lambda I gives det(A - lambda I) = 0.
Reduces the eigenvalue condition to a known determinant criterion for singularity.
proof_plan: By {{Defof|Eigenvalue of Matrix}}, $\lambda$ is an eigenvalue {{iff}} $\mathbf A \mathbf v = \lambda \mathbf v$ for some $\mathbf v \ne \mathbf 0$, that is, $\paren {\mathbf A - \lambda \mathbf I} \mathbf v = \mathbf 0$.
This holds {{iff}} $\map \ker {\mathbf A - \lambda \mathbf I} \ne \set {\mathbf 0}$, that is, $\mathbf A - \lambda \mathbf I$ is [[Definition:Singular Matrix|singular]].
By [[Matrix is Invertible iff Determinant has Multiplicative Inverse]], applied to $\mathbf M = \mathbf A - \lambda \mathbf I$, this holds {{iff}} $\map \det {\mathbf A - \lambda \mathbf I} = 0$.

Hence the eigenvalues of $\mathbf A$ are the roots of the [[Definition:Characteristic Polynomial of Matrix|characteristic polynomial]] $\map \det {\mathbf A - t \mathbf I}$.
{{qed}}
